newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, unfazed by Norilsk tender.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, unfazed by Norilsk tender.

text.p: Uncertainty over a tender for 38 percent of Russia's biggest metals group Norilsk Nickel did not affect early trade on Tuesday, dealers said, seeing steady Western buying orders supporting an otherwise quiet market.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 major shares opened barely changed after closing at 518.31 on Monday.
"I don't think the market is going to move too far," said Creditanstalt Grant director of sales Tad Berger.
"I'm seeing selective Russian and Western interest and I think we will see levels about the same through the afternoon. I'm not sure Norilsk will affect the market that much."

A commission overseeing the Norilsk tender was due to vote at 0800 GMT on whether the tender would be held. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin ordered a suspension of the tender late on Monday afternoon.
Norilsk ordinary shares eased to $14.95 at 0814 GMT after closing on Monday at $15.19 while preferred shares firmed to $12.55 from $12.50 previously.
Brunswick director Martin Diggle said the market would be eyeing developments over the tender carefully but said Western investors buying was boosting leading stock nevertheless.

"We've been seeing more Western money in the past few days than we've seen in recent weeks," Diggle said, adding fund managers worried about buying into the sky-high New York market were turning to Russia to soak up cash.
National power company UES slipped to $0.4280 after $0.4305, while oil company LUKoil edged up to $23.40 from $23.25.
He said wide discounts between ordinary and preferred shares on some stock were attracting particular interest.
